target.title: fix: await extension api.exec process-tree cleanup
target.body:
Follow-up to #98340.
Related: #98335.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the remaining lifecycle gap after #98340: extension `api.exec()` now targets the full process tree, but its timeout, abort, and default output-overflow paths can still resolve before the shared helper finishes its grace window and force-kill escalation. A wrapper may be gone while a long-lived descendant is still alive when callers receive the result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an awaited variant at the existing shared process-tree owner and has extension exec retain and await exactly one cleanup promise before resolving. Unix cleanup remains process-group based, Windows cleanup remains `taskkill /T` based with bounded waits, and existing fire-and-forget callers keep their current helper semantics. PID-less spawn failures retain the direct-child fallback.

The awaited helper stays internal to OpenClaw rather than growing the public plugin SDK surface. The implementation and commit preserve contributor credit for @ooiuuii, whose #98340 established the canonical process-tree boundary.

## User Impact

Extensions can rely on a killed `api.exec()` result to mean the wrapper and its descendants have completed bounded cleanup after timeout, abort, or default output overflow. Result codes, truncation fields, and existing error behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Exact PR head: `473706bae24e91c8e1957fa9174ecdc9c20313fd`, cleanly based on `fcb135dfc13ea346f7413d16a2c565f901f3b65c`; later `main` commits did not touch the affected exec, kill-tree, or agent-core export files.
- Exact-head hosted CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28509165828 completed successfully. The one unrelated `runtime-inventory-drift-check` QA failure passed on isolated rerun job `84506924377`; build, lint, production/test types, dependency/guard checks, all Linux test shards, CodeQL, OpenGrep, and native Windows CI are green.
- Focused process proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/exec.test.ts src/agents/sessions/exec.real.test.ts src/process/kill-tree.test.ts` passed 23 tests across 2 shards.
- Real process proof covers a wrapper plus long-lived descendant for timeout, abort, and default output overflow; the timeout descendant ignores `SIGTERM`, requiring force escalation before `execCommand()` resolves.
- Plugin SDK boundary: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check` passed at the existing 10,405 public exports / 5,223 callable exports; its 8 focused regression tests passed.
- Targeted lint: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.json ...` passed for all touched files.
- Linux Testbox-through-Crabbox: `tbx_01kwefhav9hdyzjq28rcey4rw5`, 23 tests passed, including all three real descendant lifecycle paths. Actions: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28507036195
- Windows/WSL2 best effort: WSL2 lease `cbx_75dc9acc4724` / run `run_a2458a09172a` bootstrapped but failed before project code at `write sync manifests`. Native Windows lease `cbx_1d6b5d9b5c52` / run `run_c06eb9b9847d` synced but the raw image lacked Node. Exact-head native Windows curated CI passed, but that suite does not include the new awaited-descendant tests; no direct Windows descendant-cleanup result is claimed.
- Earlier exact-head CI exposed patch-owned test-type, lint, and plugin SDK export-budget issues; all were fixed before the final run above.
- Final autoreview after rebase: genuine Codex `gpt-5.6-sol` with `xhigh` reasoning, no accepted/actionable findings, `patch is correct` (0.94 confidence); parallel focused gates exited 0.
- Formatting and whitespace: `pnpm exec oxfmt --write ...` and `git diff --check` passed.

AI-assisted implementation; the patch and process contracts were reviewed against current source, Node's documented detached-process/direct-child/spawn lifecycle behavior, and Windows `taskkill /T` behavior.
